newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU says Dutch may have broken competition rules.
newsitem.headline: EU says Dutch may have broken competition rules.

text.p: EU Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert said in a newspaper interview on Saturday the Netherlands may have broken EU rules on state aid over so-called techno-lease agreements involving financial group Rabobank and electronics giant Philips, among others.
Van Miert told the NRC Handelsblad the Dutch government should have provided the Commission with details of the deals as they could possibly be interpreted as illegal state subsidies.
"There is only one body in Europe that should judge on this, and that is the European Commission," he said. "Rules are rules and no company or government is above the law."
The agreements, forged in the early 1990s, involved firms such as Philips and Fokker selling technological know-how to Rabobank and then leasing it back.
As a result, the firms selling the know-how received a much needed cash injection and Rabobank was allowed by the Dutch government to write off the purchase sum gradually against tax.
Van Miert said the Commission was still investigating the deals and had written to the Dutch government asking for more information.
If the Commission decides the transactions amounted to illegal state aid, it has the power to order the companies involved to pay back the money.
